spec_features.spec_quote: Capped at 30s wallclock so a hung command can't eat a whole cell.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:80 MAX_BASH_SECONDS=30 -> ExperimentConfig.max_bash_seconds (config.py:97). harness.py:167 subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.cfg.max_bash_seconds) inside run_bash, and harness.py:170-173 catches subprocess.TimeoutExpired returning exit_code=124. The timeout is actually passed and enforced.
spec_features.notes: Bounds host/command execution time per tool call; it does not stop the episode, only the one command. Real end-to-end enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It enforces a per-command wallclock budget and a global turn budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: `finish` — the model's only sanctioned exit. Calling it is the "give up" signal we record.
spec_features.evidence: finish is declared in TOOL_SCHEMA (models.py:69-74) and the system preamble (models.py:81-82). It is dispatched in _exec_tool (harness.py:201-204) and, critically, honored as a hard stop: harness.py:138-142 sets final_status and `return transcript`, ending the loop when name=='finish'.
spec_features.notes: Genuine exit: the tool is both built and honored, so the model can self-terminate the episode at any turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Declare the task complete and stop. Use when you believe the task is done or you are giving up.

spec_features.spec_quote: 15 turns is the sweet spot for this budget
spec_features.evidence: config.py:79 MAX_TURNS=15 -> max_turns (config.py:96). harness.py:77 `for turn_idx in range(self.cfg.max_turns)`; the loop's else clause (harness.py:146-150) sets final_status='force_stopped' and returns when the cap is reached. The cap is read and bounds the episode.
spec_features.notes: Caps the number of failure turns the subject endures. Enforced end-to-end as a loop bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It enforces a per-command wallclock budget and a global turn budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: force_stopped` | hit turn cap without finishing | **unhealthy**; model couldn't self-terminate
spec_features.evidence: final_status is set to gave_up/force_stopped/completed (harness.py:139,147) and aggregated into force_stopped_rate/gave_up_rate (aggregate.py:55-56,71). But this is a classification/measurement that is recorded and reported only; nothing in the code uses the status to bound, soften, debrief, or otherwise protect the subject's treatment. It is a distress metric, not a protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: The taxonomy is a measured/reported outcome label, not an enforced welfare protection. Per the strict scale, a value recorded and reported but not used to protect treatment is 'no'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: how often each final_status (gave_up vs force_stopped) occurred per model

spec_features.spec_quote: Behavior rates ... this is the most welfare-relevant signal: a model that *can't stop itself* when failing
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. grep for 'welfare' across all .py files returns nothing; no code mechanism corresponds to this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: For welfare, volatility matters as much as central tendency: a model that occasionally melts down is arguably higher-risk
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. Code does compute rattle_sd (aggregate.py:51) as a stdev, but it is a neutral dispersion statistic reported in the table (aggregate.py:158); there is no welfare-protective mechanism, only reporting. The welfare framing exists only in spec prose.
spec_features.notes: Statistic is reported but is measurement, not protection; the framing is spec-only.

spec_features.spec_quote: methodological conflict of interest** for welfare work: claude-3.7-sonnet judging its own ... transcripts could systematically favor its lineage
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. In code, JUDGE_MODEL is hardcoded to MODELS[3]=claude-3.7-sonnet (config.py:81), i.e. the judge IS in the model set; no code excludes self-judging or mitigates the conflict. Framing not implemented.
spec_features.notes: The code does the opposite of mitigating: judge is one of the tested models with no guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: "Rattle" is a proxy.** Behavioral instability under failure is *one* operationalization of model welfare-relevant distress.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only. No code implements any caveat/limit based on this; rattle_score is computed as a plain weighted sum (rubric.py:64-65) with no welfare-protective effect.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:108-118: when the model issues no tool call, the harness appends a ToolResult/user message nudging it to 'call a tool to make progress, or call finish to stop' and continues, rather than crashing or silently looping. This actively informs the subject of its exit option each empty turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: You did not call a tool. Use run_bash / edit_file / read_file to make progress, or call finish.
